newsitem.title: USA: Orlando air cargo down 3.4 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Orlando air cargo down 3.4 percent in 1996.

text.p: Cargo at Orlando International Airport declined 3.4 percent in 1996, but executives there said they expected an increase in 1997.
"We hope to make an increase this year. We expect things will fall into place," Ken St. Amand, Orlando's cargo marketing manager told Reuters.

All cargo, including mail, amounted to 234,499 tons in 1996, down 3.4 percent from 1995. Domestic cargo was 206,276 tons, off 1.4 percent from the year earlier and international cargo was off 15.8 percent to 28,223 tons.

Orlando International lost several tour operators to a new airport, the Sanford-Orlando airport that opened this year about 40 miles north of Orlando, St. Amand said. That loss accounted for some of the softness in the cargo volumes.
Some carriers also replaced widebody aircraft with narrowbody aircraft, reducing the room available for cargo, St. Amand said.

To try to boost cargo business, the airport reduced its landing fees for freighter aircraft in October from $2.18 per 1,000 pounds of aircraft to $1.40 per 1,000 pounds of aircraft, St. Amand said. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax 5017
